text: EX-99.1 2 acad-ex99_1.htm EX-99.1 EX-99.1 Exhibit 99.1 Acadia Pharmaceuticals Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results - Third quarter GAAP total revenues of $342 million, up 22% year-over-year as compared to non-GAAP adjusted total revenues - Third quarter DAYBUE ® GAAP net sales of $140 million, up 39% year-over-year driven by strong uptake of DAYBUE STIX - Third quarter NUPLAZID ® GAAP net sales of $202 million, up 12% year-over-year on a non-GAAP adjusted basis - Raises 2026 DAYBUE net sales guidance to $505–$520 million; narrows NUPLAZID range and total revenue range - Additional data from Phase 3-enabling RADIANT Phase 2 Study to be presented at the Clinical Trials on Alzheimer’s Disease conference on November 17 SAN DIEGO, CA, November 4, 2026 – Acadia Pharmaceuticals Inc. (Nasdaq: ACAD), today announced its financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. “Acadia delivered a strong third quarter, with total revenues of $342 million and continued commercial momentum across DAYBUE and NUPLAZID,” said Catherine Owen Adams, Chief Executive Officer of Acadia. “In the U.S., DAYBUE delivered another strong quarter, supported by meaningful uptake of DAYBUE STIX. In Europe, we are excited to build momentum following our recent launch of DAYBU in Germany. NUPLAZID also performed well, driven by underlying demand and the continued expansion of our commercial reach. Together, these growing franchises provide the commercial and financial foundation to advance clinical programs with the potential to become Acadia’s next meaningful growth opportunities. In Alzheimer’s disease psychosis, we are continuing Phase 3 development of remlifanserin based on Phase 2 results. As we look ahead to 2027, we anticipate two Phase 2 readouts: ACP-211 in major depressive disorder, and remlifanserin in Lewy body dementia psychosis, for which we are providing timing guidance for the first time. We look forward to sharing these updates as we continue to advance the next wave of our pipeline.” Company Updates • Announced Phase 3-enabling topline results from the Phase 2 RADIANT study of remlifanserin in Alzheimer’s disease psychosis, with consistent efficacy trends at the 60 mg dose across all four psychosis scales that were assessed for the full study population and a favorable safety and tolerability profile supporting continued and optimized Phase 3 development. Additional data will be presented at the Clinical Trials on Alzheimer’s Disease conference on November 17, 2026, in Boston. • Two Phase 2 readouts anticipated in 2027: ACP-211 in major depressive disorder (MDD) in the second half and, for the first time, guidance for remlifanserin in Lewy body dementia Psychosis (LBDP) in the fourth quarter. • Received FDA Fast Track designation for remlifanserin for the treatment of Lewy body dementia psychosis, recognizing the significant unmet need for new treatment options. • Received allowance of a new U.S. patent covering weight-banded dosing of trofinetide, extending U.S. patent protections for DAYBUE and DAYBUE STIX by nearly five years, through March 2041. • Received European Commission approval for DAYBU ® (trofinetide) as the first and only treatment for the neurobehavioral symptoms of Rett syndrome in adults and pediatric patients aged five years and older in the European Union in August 2026 and launched DAYBU in Germany in early October 2026 with patients already receiving commercial product. • Completed the Phase 3 study of trofinetide in Rett syndrome in Japan, with results consistent with the LAVENDER Phase 3 study and supportive of a planned regulatory filing; Acadia continues to pursue a distribution partner in preparation for regulatory filing in 2027 and a potential launch in 2028, subject to regulatory approval. Financial Results Revenues GAAP total revenues, consisting of net product sales from NUPLAZID and DAYBUE, were $342 million in the third quarter of 2026, up 23% as compared to GAAP total revenues of $279 million in the third quarter of 2025, and up 22% as compared to non-GAAP adjusted total revenues of $281 million in the third quarter of 2025. GAAP net product sales of NUPLAZID were $202 million in the third quarter of 2026, up 14% as compared to GAAP net product sales of $178 million in the third quarter of 2025, and up 12% as compared to non-GAAP adjusted net product sales of $180 million in the third quarter of 2025. Net product sales of DAYBUE were $140 million in the third quarter of 2026, an increase of 39% as compared to $101 million in the third quarter of 2025. A reconciliation of NUPLAZID non-GAAP adjusted net product sales and non-GAAP adjusted total revenues is provided in Table 1. A description of these adjustments is included under ‘Non-GAAP Financial Measures.’ Research and Development Research and development expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were $76 million, as compared to $88 million for the same period of 2025. Selling, General and Administrative Selling, general and administrative expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were $159 million, as compared to $133 million for the same period of 2025. Net Income For the third quarter of 2026, Acadia reported net income of $54 million, or $0.31 per diluted share, as compared to net income of $72 million, or $0.42 per diluted share, for the same period of 2025. Cash and Investments At September 30, 2026, Acadia’s cash, cash equivalents, and investment securities totaled $976 million, as compared to $820 million at December 31, 2025. Full Year 2026 Financial Guidance (GAAP): Acadia is updating its 2026 guidance: • Total revenues revised to a range of $1.265 to $1.295 billion, compared with a previous range of $1.24 to $1.30 billion. • NUPLAZID net product sales narrowed to a range of $760 to $775 million, compared with the previous guidance range of $760 to $790 million. • DAYBUE (including all forms of trofinetide) global net product sales in the range of $505 to $520 million, up from the previous range of $480 to $510 million. • R&D expense in the range of $325 to $340 million, down from the previous range of $355 to $380 million. • SG&A expense in the range of $665 to $685 million, compared with the previous guidance range of $660 to $700 million. About NUPLAZID ® (pimavanserin) Pimavanserin is a selective serotonin inverse agonist and antagonist preferentially targeting 5-HT2A receptors. These receptors are thought to play an important role in neuropsychiatric disorders. In vitro, pimavanserin demonstrated no appreciable binding affinity for dopamine (including D2), histamine, muscarinic, or adrenergic receptors. Pimavanserin was approved for the treatment of hallucinations and delusions associated with Parkinson’s disease psychosis by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in April 2016 under the trade name NUPLAZID. About DAYBUE ® (trofinetide) Trofinetide is a synthetic version of a naturally occurring molecule known as the tripeptide glycine-proline-glutamate (GPE). The mechanism by which trofinetide exerts therapeutic effects in patients with Rett syndrome is unknown. Trofinetide was first approved for the treatment of Rett syndrome in adults and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in March 2023 under the trade name DAYBUE. Trofinetide is approved for use under the name DAYBUE ® and DAYBUE ® STIX in the United States and under the name DAYBUE ® in Canada and DAYBU ® in the European Union. References to DAYBUE net product sales include global net product sales of all commercially available forms of trofinetide, including those referenced above. About Acadia Pharmaceuticals Acadia is committed to turning scientific promise into meaningful innovation that makes the difference for underserved neurological and rare disease communities around the world. Our commercial portfolio includes the first and only FDA-approved treatments for Parkinson’s disease psychosis and Rett syndrome. We are developing the next wave of therapeutic advancements with a robust and diverse pipeline that includes mid- to late-stage programs in Alzheimer’s disease psychosis and Lewy body dementia psychosis, along with earlier-stage programs that address other underserved patient needs. At Acadia, we’re here to be their difference. For more information, visit us at acadia.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X .
